unlisted_practices: Pairing machine-learning mortality risk predictions with behavioral-economics nudges to prompt clinicians to hold serious illness conversations, evaluated for effects on end-of-life spending

models_evaluated: Unnamed machine-learning algorithm identifying high risk of 180-day mortality

links.outcome: Mean daily end-of-life spending with risk-informed prompts for serious illness conversations versus standard care
links.effect: Mean daily spending was $377.96 vs. $449.92; adjusted mean difference, -$75.33; 95% confidence interval, -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02. Adjusted savings were $13,747 per decedent.
links.quote: The intervention was associated with lower unadjusted mean daily spending in the last 6 months of life for the intervention group versus controls ($377.96 vs. $449.92; adjusted mean difference, -$75.33; 95% confidence interval, -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02), translating to $13,747 total adjusted savings per decedent and $13 million in cumulative savings across all decedents in the intervention group.
